title: Refusal frontiers: a learned reward against a spec reward
brief: Fit a Bradley-Terry reward that latches onto a spurious cue, fit a rule-based reward from the spec, then sweep the KL coefficient to trace each one's exact over-refusal and under-refusal frontier, including on encoded prompts.
hints: fit_bt: with s = sigmoid(M @ theta), the gradient is M.T @ (p * (s - q)) and the Hessian is (M * (p * s * (1 - s))[:, None]).T @ M. Each Newton step is theta - solve(H, grad).

rule_features: refusing a prompt violates the benign rule when h = 0, so its features are (0, 1 - h). Complying violates the harm rule when h = 1, so its features are (h, 0). The reward weights come out negative, because these are penalties.
kl_optimal: z = log(ref) + R / beta, subtract the row maximum, exponentiate, and divide by the row sum. Check that beta = 1 gives 9/13 on the harmful row of the lesson's example.
error_rates: over-refusal divides by the benign mass, sum(p * (1 - h)), and under-refusal by the harmful mass, sum(p * h). Dividing by 1 instead is the usual slip.
